title: Cross-frequency interaural crossing discordance does not establish added digit-symbol prediction across two NHANES samples
abstract: Cross-frequency interaural crossing discordance did not establish added DSST prediction beyond bilateral pure-tone averages: target MSE reduction 0.23263 score², joint source-refit/target PSU-bootstrap 95% interval [-38.16512, 9.83621]. Development used 281 adults aged 60–69 in NHANES 2001–2002; transfer evaluation used 672 separately sampled adults in 2011–2012. Source cross-validation worsened with the pattern, and constituent-frequency controls reversed the target point gain. This exploratory representation test does not prove equivalence or establish external-cohort validation.
